analysis.title: Galaxy Digital Inc. (GLXY): First Take: Revenue beat driven by digital asset gains; questions on timing of Helios II contract
key_insights: GLXY reported 3Q26 diluted EPS of $0.83 vs GSe $0.54 and Visible Alpha consensus $0.18. Core adj. EPS (ex-SBC, normalized tax) was $0.74 vs GSe $0.58 and consensus $0.26.
Net revenue was 87% above consensus and 20% above GSe. The beat came mainly from Treasury and Corporate net revenue (26% above GSe) and Digital assets net revenue (11% above GSe).

Much of the top-line beat came from larger unrealized digital asset gains in Treasury and Corporate, which follow crypto prices. GS expects a modestly positive reaction given the broad-based revenue beat.

Adj. operating margin was 58.2%, 17.5pp ahead of the Street and in line with GSe. Adj. operating expenses (ex-SBC) were 20% above consensus. Adj. EBITDA of $455mn was 125% above the Street and 26% above GSe.

Global markets net revenue of $53mn rose 8% QoQ and was 18% above GSe on 12% higher volumes QoQ. Management said GLXY volume growth outperformed broader spot market volume declines. The average loan book grew 27% QoQ on financing demand.

Asset management net revenue of $19mn rose 11% QoQ, fell 19% YoY and was 4% below GSe. EOP AUS of about $4.6bn was up 64% QoQ and down 31% YoY. ETF AUM was $2.5bn and Alternatives $3.3bn, up 41% and 30% QoQ on higher digital asset prices and the launch of the Galaxy Sharplink Onchain Yield Fund. Total AUM and AUS on platform rose $3.3bn QoQ to $10.4bn.
GLXY added to balance sheet digital assets. At 3Q26 vs 2Q26 it held net BTC exposure of $538mn vs $400mn, ETH $128mn vs 0, SOL $108mn vs $58mn and net other digital assets $102mn vs $95mn.

Data centers recognized $79mn net revenue, in line with GSe. Helios I Phase II construction is on schedule with delivery expected in 2Q27. The roughly 830MW of approved Helios II capacity has no tenant yet, which GS expects to remain an investor focus.

GS wants clarity on the data center expansion outlook, any impact from rising funding costs across the AI data center ecosystem, what drove Global markets outperformance and its outlook, and the asset management net flow outlook given modest industry ETF outflows QTD.

GS is Neutral with a $24 12-month price target (price $15.68, 53.1% upside), set on a SOTP: 23.5x adj. P/E (ex-SBC) for Digital assets, 13.5x EV/adj. EBITDA (ex-SBC) for Data centers and 1x tangible book for Treasury and corporate.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral rating and $24 12-month target kept after 3Q26 results. The target rests on a SOTP valuation across Digital assets, Data centers and Treasury and corporate.

earnings_insights: GLXY 3Q26 diluted EPS $0.83 reported vs GSe estimate $0.54 and Visible Alpha consensus estimate $0.18, reported 10/27/2026 (GS uses its own share count because consensus submissions are widely dispersed).
GLXY 3Q26 core adj. EPS $0.74 reported (ex-SBC, normalized tax rate) vs GSe estimate $0.58 and consensus estimate $0.26.
GLXY 3Q26 net revenue was 87% above consensus and 20% above GSe. Treasury and Corporate net revenue was $419mn reported, 26% above GSe, on unrealized gains on digital assets and investment positions.
GLXY 3Q26 adj. EBITDA $455mn reported, 125% above the Street and 26% above GSe. Adj. operating margin was 58.2% reported.

GS estimates: 12/26E EPS $0.04, 12/27E EPS $(0.26), 12/28E EPS $0.12. Revenue estimates are $632.6mn for 2026E, $1,086.5mn for 2027E and $1,722.6mn for 2028E. The 4Q26E EPS estimate is $(0.02) and 1Q27E is $(0.07).
crypto_views: GLXY volume growth of 12% QoQ outperformed broader spot crypto volume declines, per management.

GS lists upside risks as favorable crypto regulation, higher crypto market cap and faster institutional uptake of digital assets activity. Downside risks are crypto market volatility and persistently lower crypto market cap.
Industry ETF flows show modest outflows QTD, which GS flags as relevant to the asset management net flow outlook.
risk_factors: Crypto market volatility and persistently lower crypto market cap.
Slowing AI investment and data center oversupply.
The 830MW of Helios II capacity remains uncontracted.
Higher funding costs across the AI data center ecosystem could affect GLXY.
Much of the revenue beat depends on unrealized digital asset gains tied to crypto prices.

tension_points.bull_case: Broad-based net revenue beat of 87% vs consensus and 20% vs GSe, with trading volumes outperforming industry trends and Helios I Phase II on schedule for 2Q27 delivery.
tension_points.bear_case: Much of the top-line beat came from larger unrealized digital asset gains in Treasury and Corporate, which depend on crypto prices. The 830MW of Helios II capacity has no tenant.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A signing of a Helios II tenant would ease the data center concern. Lower crypto prices would reverse the Treasury and Corporate gains.

theme_stances.key_argument: The company has yet to find a tenant for its 830MW of approved Helios II capacity, which GS expects to remain an investor focus.
